uncited: The NTS Training Objective is a composite loss function designed to optimize UV volumes and neural texture stack parameters for real-time rendering of human performances.
It solves the problem of training differentiable radiance fields by combining photometric, perceptual, semantic, UV-metric, and silhouette losses.
The method optimizes the model parameters by minimizing a weighted sum of five distinct loss terms.

*   **Inputs:** Ground-truth image $\mathcal{I}$, ground-truth binary human mask $\mathcal{S}$, DensePose outputs (semantic probability $\mathcal{P}_k$, UV coordinates $\mathcal{U}_k, \mathcal{V}_k$ for $k=1 \dots N_k$), and rendered image $\hat{\mathcal{I}}$.
*   $\hat{\mathcal{P}}_k, \hat{\mathcal{U}}_k, \hat{\mathcal{V}}_k$: Predicted semantic probability and UV coordinates for body part $k$.
*   **Noisy DensePose Supervision:** DensePose outputs may contain incorrect semantic and UV labels.
*   **Mask Definition:** The binary mask $\mathcal{S}$ must strictly follow the convention: 0 for foreground (human) and 1 for background.
It is part of a framework for real-time rendering of human performances, utilizing UV volumes to store appearance and geometry information.

The method was developed to address the limitations of patch-based training and to leverage pseudo-supervision from pre-trained models like DensePose to regularize the solution space of UV volumes [S1].

The claim states that the method was developed to address the limitations of patch-based training and to leverage pseudo-supervision from pre-trained models like DensePose to regularize the solution space of UV volumes. Source [S1] explicitly supports both parts of this claim: 1) It states, 'Benefiting from our memory-saving framework... we can render an entire image during training instead of sampling image patches,' addressing the limitation of patch-based methods. 2) It states, 'To warm-start the UV volumes and regularize its solution space, we leverage the pre-trained DensePose model as an auxiliary supervisor... utilize the outputs of Denspose as pseudo supervision,' directly supporting the second part of the claim.
